resources.string: Uncompressed: lowest delay and perfect quality. Uses about 1.5 Mbit/s, which is nothing for home Wi-Fi.\n\nCompressed (Opus): a tenth of the data, but about 27 ms more delay. Only worth it on weak Wi-Fi.
Only used with Compressed. 128 kbps is plenty for TV and movies; 192–256 kbps is for music.
Mono mixes left and right into one and halves the data. Handy with a single earbud.

Audio held in reserve to ride out Wi-Fi hiccups. Bigger means fewer dropouts but more delay.\n\nAuto grows after a dropout and shrinks again when things are smooth. Pick a fixed size if you need the delay to stay constant, e.g. for Kodi sync.

Low latency: Android's fast audio path. Least delay, but EQ and other audio effects are skipped.

Normal: audio effects work, slightly more delay.

Power saving: big buffers, much more delay. Music only.

Takes exclusive use of the phone\'s audio hardware, skipping Android\'s mixer. Can save another 5–10 ms.\n\nNot every phone allows it (the Listen tab shows if it worked), and it doesn\'t apply to Bluetooth.

After a Wi-Fi hiccup you can end up further behind the TV. This decides how to get back.

Aggressive: skips back at once with a tiny dip.
Normal: plays up to 2% faster for about a second.
Gentle: plays 0.4% faster, inaudible but slow.

There's no Off, because the extra delay would never go away.
The TV sends each packet again 10 ms later, so if Wi-Fi drops one the copy usually gets through. Far fewer skips, twice the data (still small).
Android only uses its fastest Wi-Fi mode while the screen is on and this app is open. Dimming is fine.
Leaving the app while listening shrinks it to a small window. That keeps Wi-Fi in its fastest mode while you use other apps.
Only needed if the phone can\'t find the TV by itself. TV Relay on the TV shows it under Start streaming.

Makes Kodi play its audio early so the sound on your phone matches the picture. Each change makes Kodi catch the picture up for a moment (it skips a few frames).

Automatic: follows the measured delay, plus your adjustment, whenever it moves by about 50 ms, even mid-scene.
Automatic, at pause: the same, but only when a video starts and when you pause, so never mid-scene. Sync now applies it straight away.
Manual: only your adjustment.

Your own adjustments always apply straight away.
Move right if the sound is late, left if it\'s early.\n\nKodi only takes 25 ms steps; the phone covers the rest, so you get 5 ms precision.

Shows TV mode / Client mode on the Listen tab and on the TV screen, for when the app guesses wrong whether a device is a TV. TV mode captures and sends audio; Client mode listens.\n\nTurning this off makes you a normal user again: the automatic guess is back, and this switch is hidden until you tap the version in the update dialog 7 times again. On a TV in TV mode, switch to Client mode first to reach this setting.
When you tap Stop, the TV keeps capturing so the next Listen starts straight away, without the TV\'s recording prompt.\n\nOff: Stop asks whether to stop the TV too.
Puts Mode and Adjustment on the Listen tab too, above the graph, so you can fine-tune while watching.
Turn on if moving the slider right makes the sound later instead of earlier.
